original_question: For integers m and n, determine necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of an F_p-vector space L_{m+1,n} of dimension n whose nonzero elements are logarithmic differential forms on P^1 with a unique zero at infinity of order m - 1. In particular, if n >= 2 and such a space exists, must p^(n-1)(p - 1) divide m + 1?
target_in_paper: The draft is trying to capture Pagot's conjectural existence criterion for spaces L_{m+1,n}: an F_p-vector space L_{m+1,n} should exist exactly when p^(n-1)(p-1) divides m+1, together with the nearby necessary condition m+1 = λ p^(n-1) from Proposition 1.2 and the verified cases n = 2 with m+1 = p, 2p, 3p from Theorem 1.3. The arXiv identifier in your prompt resolves to a different workshop-problems paper, so the mathematical target matching your draft is Pagot's arXiv:math/0203259. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0203259))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main object (an n-dimensional F_p-vector space L_{m+1,n} of logarithmic differential forms on P^1), the condition that every nonzero form has a unique zero at infinity of order m-1, and the intended divisibility criterion as the core issue. It is aimed at the paper's central existence problem, not a side remark. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0203259))
missing_details: The paper works over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p > 0, with p prime; this ambient field should be part of a stand-alone formulation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0203259))
The quantified variables are positive integers n,m, and the paper assumes gcd(m,p)=1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0203259))

A 'logarithmic differential form' here means a form of the shape ω = df/f for some f in k(P^1)^×, not merely an arbitrary meromorphic 1-form with a zero condition. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/9011309/contributions-to-arithmetic-geometry-in-mixed-characteris...))

The official target is conjectural and biconditional: the paper asks for an if-and-only-if existence criterion, not only whether one divisibility condition is necessary. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/9011309/contributions-to-arithmetic-geometry-in-mixed-characteris...))

Nearby context supplies the proven necessary reduction m+1 = λ p^(n-1); without that, the question misses the paper's main normalization of parameters. ([math.u-bordeaux.fr](https://www.math.u-bordeaux.fr/~mmatigno/Spaces_L_m_1_n-31.pdf))
The notation L_{m+1,n} itself should be defined explicitly as the name of the space being sought. ([math.u-bordeaux.fr](https://www.math.u-bordeaux.fr/~mmatigno/Spaces_L_m_1_n-31.pdf))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should be read against the proven cases n = 2 and m+1 = p, 2p, 3p recorded near the conjecture. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/9011309/contributions-to-arithmetic-geometry-in-mixed-characteris...))

After imposing Proposition 1.2, the conjecture can be rewritten in terms of λ = (m+1)/p^(n-1); that equivalent parametrization is implicit in your draft but explicit in the nearby discussion. ([math.u-bordeaux.fr](https://www.math.u-bordeaux.fr/~mmatigno/Spaces_L_m_1_n-31.pdf))
refined_question: Let p be a prime, k an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, and let n,m be positive integers with gcd(m,p)=1. Does there exist an n-dimensional F_p-vector space L_{m+1,n} of meromorphic differential forms on P^1_k such that every nonzero ω in L_{m+1,n} is logarithmic (i.e. ω = df/f for some f in k(P^1)^×) and has a unique zero at infinity of order m-1? If so, is Pagot's conjectural criterion true, namely that such a space exists if and only if p^(n-1)(p-1) divides m+1? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0203259))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using Proposition 1.2 to write necessarily m+1 = λ p^(n-1), determine whether spaces L_{λ p^(n-1),n} exist exactly for those triples (p,n,λ) with p-1 dividing λ. ([math.u-bordeaux.fr](https://www.math.u-bordeaux.fr/~mmatigno/Spaces_L_m_1_n-31.pdf))
justification: The draft is close to the paper's main question but omits several paper-critical hypotheses and the exact conjectural form. Later sources explicitly identify Pagot's original result package as follows: Proposition 1.2 gives the necessary condition m+1 = λ p^(n-1); §2.3, Remarque 2 states the conjecture that existence should be equivalent to p^(n-1)(p-1) dividing m+1; and the early theorem proves this in the cases n = 2 and m+1 = p, 2p, 3p. Those are exactly the ingredients your draft is trying to capture. Because arXiv:math/0411059 is a different proceedings volume, the mathematically matching source is Pagot's paper arXiv:math/0203259. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0203259))
